title: How to use AI for consulting work
description: Use Strawberry across client research, proposals, meetings, recommendations, and follow-through while keeping evidence and approvals clear.

navigation.title: Consulting
navigation.tagline: Client research, proposals, delivery, and follow-through

introduction: Most consultants already have plenty of context. It is spread across meeting notes, email threads, an RFP portal, research tabs, and past deliverables. The tedious part is bringing the right pieces into the next decision without rebuilding the project each time.

Strawberry works in the same visible browser as that material. Your companion can use what is already open or connected, follow research into logged-in sites, and carry what matters into a proposal, recommendation, brief, or deck without rebuilding the engagement for each new task.

blocks.text: Not sure where to begin? Your companion can look at the client work you have open and suggest a useful skill to try first.

skill.context: Find a useful starting point for your consulting work and complete one real result.

blocks.text: A market map, company list, or interview summary usually gets the client only partway. They still need credible options, the tradeoffs between them, and a recommendation they can challenge.

Your companion chooses the right research path: mapping an unfamiliar market, extracting repeated data across many pages, investigating a company, or comparing a smaller set visually. Because the research happens in Strawberry's visible browser workspace, you can inspect the sources, correct the direction, or take over in a logged-in site while it works.

The recommendation keeps evidence, client claims, calculations, and inference distinct. It can become a memo, deck, workshop artifact, or supporting spreadsheet, depending on how the client will make the decision.

items.title: Build the recommendation
items.text: Turn the research into credible options and a defensible recommendation, keeping the evidence, client claims, calculations, tradeoffs, and inference clear in the artifact the decision needs.

skill.context: Research this company around the client question I need to answer.

items.title: Collect repeated web evidence at scale

sections.title: Move cleanly from sale to delivery

blocks.text: Before the client accepts the work, the proposal says what is being promised: the intended outcomes, work, responsibilities, timeline, fees, and terms. Strawberry uses the real opportunity record and leaves missing pricing, authority, ROI, or legal language visible instead of guessing.

After acceptance, the same reviewed context becomes the engagement brief, including the scope, stakeholders, milestones, evidence standards, and client restrictions. The delivery team does not have to reconstruct the agreement during kickoff.

items.title: Define what is being promised
items.text: Turn the real opportunity or RFP into the outcomes, work, responsibilities, timeline, fees, terms, and open questions.

skill.context: Turn an opportunity or RFP into a complete commercial and delivery proposal ready for review.

items.title: Turn the proposal into an engagement brief
items.text: Carry the scope, stakeholders, milestones, evidence standards, and client restrictions into one engagement brief.

skill.context: Start accepted work with one reliable engagement brief.

sections.title: Use meetings to keep the work moving

blocks.text: Before a meeting, Strawberry can start from the calendar and pull in the few decisions, commitments, documents, or changes that should affect the conversation. After a reliable transcript or set of notes is available, the debrief separates discussion from decisions and turns accepted commitments into proposed follow-through.

A daily brief connects that meeting loop to the rest of the consultant's work: which calls need preparation, which promises are due, and which risks or messages deserve attention. Follow-up emails, status updates, CRM changes, and project updates stay separately reviewable.

items.title: See what needs attention across clients
items.text: Bring today's client calls, messages, commitments, risks, and decisions into one concise view.

skill.context: See which clients, meetings, messages, commitments, and risks deserve attention today.

items.title: Walk into the meeting prepared
items.text: Pull together the few decisions, commitments, documents, and changes that should shape a client, workshop, steering, delivery, or internal meeting.

skill.context: Prepare a concise brief for an upcoming client, workshop, steering, delivery, or internal meeting.

items.title: Turn the conversation into follow-through
items.text: Separate discussion from decisions, capture commitments and actions, and prepare the right follow-up or system update for review.

skill.context: Turn a completed meeting into decisions, commitments, actions, and controlled follow-through.

blocks.text: Feedback helps your companion learn which sources you trust, what a useful result looks like, and how you want drafts reviewed. Once the method works, save it as a custom skill or a sanitized team skill. Client details stay with the client they belong to.

items: Share an approved artifact when someone only needs the result.
Share a sanitized team skill when colleagues need the method but not another client's context.
Create a Routine when the sources, trigger, output, ownership, and review step have settled.
